programme.subtitle: Build, access, inspect, protect, snapshot, and remove a single Amazon Linux 2023 instance
programme.description: Starting with an administrator-capable AWS sign-in and no learner infrastructure, create a dedicated IAM learner identity, a small public VPC network, an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance, and a Systems Manager Session Manager connection. Install Apache, inspect the instance and its EBS storage, test stop/start behavior, create an EBS snapshot, and remove only the resources created for this lab.
programme.learningOutcome: Create and operate a securely managed Amazon EC2 instance in eu-west-2, explain its VPC, subnet, routing, security group, IAM role, addressing, instance lifecycle, EBS volume, and snapshot choices in SAA-C03 terms, and clean up the entire lab.

phases.title: Phase 1: Establish the learner identity
phases.description: Create a dedicated IAM user, grant only the lab capabilities, sign in as that user, and verify the AWS CLI identity.

phases.title: Phase 2: Build isolated network foundations
phases.description: Create a VPC, public subnet, internet gateway, public route table, and security group before launching compute.

phases.title: Phase 3: Launch a managed EC2 workload
phases.description: Create the Systems Manager EC2 role and launch Amazon Linux 2023 with the required network and storage settings.

phases.title: Phase 4: Connect and publish a test website
phases.description: Use Session Manager rather than SSH, install Apache, and test browser access through the deliberately narrow HTTP rule.

phases.title: Phase 5: Inspect, operate, protect, and remove
phases.description: Examine instance and EBS details, test stop/start behavior, create a recovery snapshot, verify it, and clean up.

tasks.title: Create the dedicated training IAM user and verify its CLI identity
tasks.feature: IAM user, console sign-in, and programmatic CLI access
tasks.goal: Create fa-ec2-learner, give it a policy limited to the named EC2 lab resources and the fixed SSM instance role/profile, create console and CLI credentials, and verify the CLI identity.
tasks.whyItMatters: The administrator performs initial identity setup. The learner then uses a separate IAM user with only the permissions required to create, operate, inspect, and remove this lab's VPC, EC2, EBS, and Systems Manager resources.

consoleSteps.title: Create the learner user and restricted policy as an administrator
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an administrator-capable identity. Do not perform this setup while signed in as the future learner user.

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console using an administrator-capable identity. Do not perform this setup while signed in as the future learner user.
In the top navigation search box, enter IAM, then choose IAM.
In the left navigation pane, choose Users, then choose Create user.
For User name, enter fa-ec2-learner.
Select Provide user access to the AWS Management Console.
Select I want to create an IAM user.
Select Custom password, enter a unique password, and select Users must create a new password at next sign-in.
Choose Next, select Attach policies directly, then choose Create policy.
Choose the JSON tab, replace all editor content with the supplied policy JSON, then choose Next.
For Policy name, enter fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy. Choose Create policy.
Return to the Create user browser tab. Choose the refresh control beside the policy list, select fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy, choose Next, then choose Create user.
Choose the fa-ec2-learner user name. Record the Console sign-in URL shown on the user page as [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. This is the account-specific URL used in the next step.
Choose Security credentials. Under Access keys, choose Create access key.
Select Command Line Interface (CLI), select the confirmation checkbox, choose Next, then choose Create access key.

Download the CSV or store the access key ID and secret access key in a secure password manager. The access key ID identifies the credential; the secret access key is shown only once and authenticates CLI requests.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-learner exists, has fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy attached, has console access, and has one new CLI access key.
consoleSteps.warning: Never share the password, secret access key, downloaded CSV, or CloudShell credential files. The policy deliberately permits only the named lab role/profile to be passed to EC2.

consoleSteps.title: Sign in as the learner and create the CLI profile
consoleSteps.instruction: Open a private browser window and browse to [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] is the account-specific IAM user sign-in URL recorded in the previous step.

instructions.text: Open a private browser window and browse to [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL]. [IAM_SIGN_IN_URL] is the account-specific IAM user sign-in URL recorded in the previous step.
Enter fa-ec2-learner for IAM user name and enter the password created for this user.
Complete the required password change.
Open CloudShell from the console navigation bar.
At the CloudShell prompt, run the aws configure command in the CLI route below.
When prompted, enter the fa-ec2-learner access key ID and secret access key created in the preceding step. Enter eu-west-2 for Default region name and json for Default output format.
Run the get-caller-identity command in the CLI route below. Record Account as [ACCOUNT_ID] only if you need to identify the account later.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The identity response contains an ARN ending in user/fa-ec2-learner.
consoleSteps.warning: aws configure stores credentials in the CloudShell home directory. Remove the profile after cleanup if the CloudShell environment will continue to be used.

cliSteps.explanation: Run as the original administrator to create the learner identity.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global; do not specify a Region.

cliSteps.explanation: Run after securely obtaining the learner access key. Supply credentials only at prompts, use eu-west-2 as the default Region, and use json as the default output format.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The profile is written after all prompts complete.
cliSteps.warning: Do not place credential values on the command line.

cliSteps.explanation: Confirm that subsequent CLI commands use the dedicated learner identity.
cliSteps.warning: Do not continue with the learner CLI route if the ARN identifies the administrator instead.

verification.title: Verify the active learner identity
verification.instruction: Run aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-ec2-learner in CloudShell or a local terminal.
verification.expectedResult: The returned ARN ends in user/fa-ec2-learner rather than identifying the administrator.

tasks.title: Create the VPC, public subnet, gateway, route table, and web security group
tasks.goal: Build an isolated 10.0.0.0/16 VPC with one public 10.0.1.0/24 subnet and a security group that permits browser HTTP traffic only from the learner's current public IPv4 address.
tasks.whyItMatters: For SAA-C03, a subnet becomes public because its associated route table has a route to an internet gateway; assigning a public IPv4 address alone is not enough. Security groups are stateful virtual firewalls attached to the instance network interface.

consoleSteps.title: Create the VPC and public subnet
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC.

instructions.text: ☐ In the AWS Console search box, enter VPC.
☐ Choose VPC.
☐ Confirm Region is Europe (London) eu-west-2.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Your VPCs.
☐ Choose Create VPC.
☐ Select VPC only.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-vpc in Name tag - optional.
☐ Enter 10.0.0.0/16 in IPv4 CIDR block.
☐ Leave IPv6 CIDR block set to No IPv6 CIDR block.
☐ Leave Tenancy set to Default.
☐ Choose Create VPC.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Subnets.
☐ Choose Create subnet.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC ID.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-public-subnet in Subnet name.
☐ Select eu-west-2a in Availability Zone.
☐ Enter 10.0.1.0/24 in IPv4 VPC CIDR block.
☐ Choose Create subnet.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-subnet.
☐ Choose Actions.
☐ Choose Edit subnet settings.
☐ Select Enable auto-assign public IPv4 address.
☐ Choose Save.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The VPC has CIDR 10.0.0.0/16. The subnet has CIDR 10.0.1.0/24 in eu-west-2a and automatically assigns public IPv4 addresses to launched instances.
consoleSteps.warning: Availability Zone names can be mapped differently between AWS accounts. If eu-west-2a is unavailable in the selector, use the first available eu-west-2 Availability Zone and record it as [LAB_AZ].

consoleSteps.title: Create public routing and the security group
consoleSteps.instruction: ☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Internet gateways.

instructions.text: ☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Internet gateways.
☐ Choose Create internet gateway.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-igw in Name tag.
☐ Choose Create internet gateway.
☐ Choose Actions.
☐ Choose Attach to VPC.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc.
☐ Choose Attach internet gateway.
☐ In the left navigation pane, choose Route tables.
☐ Choose Create route table.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-public-rt in Name tag.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC.
☐ Choose Create route table.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-rt.
☐ Choose the Routes tab.
☐ Choose Edit routes.
☐ Choose Add route.
☐ Enter 0.0.0.0/0 in Destination.
☐ Select Internet Gateway in Target.
☐ Select fa-ec2-igw in Internet Gateway.
☐ Choose Save changes.
☐ Choose the Subnet associations tab.
☐ Choose Edit subnet associations.
☐ Select fa-ec2-public-subnet.
☐ Choose Save associations.
☐ In the VPC left navigation pane, choose Security groups.
☐ Choose Create security group.
☐ Enter fa-ec2-web-sg in Security group name.
☐ Enter HTTP access for the fa-ec2 training website in Description.
☐ Select fa-ec2-vpc in VPC.
☐ Under Inbound rules, choose Add rule.
☐ Select HTTP in Type.
☐ Select My IP in Source.
☐ Choose Create security group.
☐ Record the Security group ID value on the security group details page as [WEB_SG_ID].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 route whose target is fa-ec2-igw and is associated with fa-ec2-public-subnet. fa-ec2-web-sg permits TCP port 80 only from the IP address detected by the console.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not add SSH port 22. Session Manager will provide administrative access without an inbound management port.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the isolated lab VPC. Record VpcId from the response as [VPC_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a Vpc object and its VpcId.
cliSteps.warning: Use [VPC_ID] only after recording it from this response.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --cidr-block 10.0.1.0/24 --availability-zone eu-west-2a --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-public-subnet}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the one public-subnet candidate. Record SubnetId as [SUBNET_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains SubnetId and AvailabilityZone eu-west-2a.
cliSteps.warning: Replace [VPC_ID] with the recorded VPC ID.

cliSteps.explanation: Make instances launched in this subnet receive a public IPv4 address, subject to public routing.
cliSteps.warning: This does not itself create internet connectivity; the route table still needs the gateway route.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the VPC internet gateway. Record InternetGatewayId as [IGW_ID].
cliSteps.warning: The gateway is not usable by the VPC until attached.

cliSteps.explanation: Attach the named lab gateway to the lab VPC.
cliSteps.warning: Replace both placeholders using earlier responses.

cliSteps.explanation: Create a separate route table for the public subnet. Record RouteTableId as [RTB_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Do not use the VPC main route table for this training example.

cliSteps.explanation: Add the default IPv4 route to the attached internet gateway.
cliSteps.warning: This route makes the associated subnet public.

cliSteps.explanation: Associate the public route table with the lab subnet.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains an AssociationId; record it as [RTB_ASSOCIATION_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Do not disassociate the VPC main route-table association.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-ec2-web-sg --description 'HTTP access for the fa-ec2 training website' --vpc-id [VPC_ID] --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-web-sg}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create the security group attached to the lab VPC. Record GroupId as [WEB_SG_ID].
cliSteps.warning: A new security group has no inbound rules until the next command.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id [WEB_SG_ID] --ip-permissions 'IpProtocol=tcp,FromPort=80,ToPort=80,IpRanges=[{CidrIp=[YOUR_PUBLIC_IPV4_CIDR],Description="Learner browser HTTP"}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Allow only browser HTTP from your current public IPv4 address. Replace [YOUR_PUBLIC_IPV4_CIDR] with the address displayed by the console My IP selector followed by /32, for example 198.51.100.10/32.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response reports the added inbound permission.
cliSteps.warning: Do not use 0.0.0.0/0 for this learner web-server test.

verification.title: Verify public-network ingredients
verification.instruction: In the VPC console, open fa-ec2-public-rt and inspect its Routes and Subnet associations tabs; then open fa-ec2-web-sg and inspect Inbound rules.
verification.expectedResult: The route table associates fa-ec2-public-subnet and routes 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-ec2-igw. The security group has only the HTTP port 80 rule from your /32 source.

tasks.title: Create the Session Manager role and launch Amazon Linux 2023
tasks.feature: IAM instance profile and Amazon EC2
tasks.goal: Create the fixed EC2 Systems Manager role and instance profile, wait until the profile is available, then launch one Amazon Linux 2023 t3.micro instance in the dedicated public subnet.
tasks.whyItMatters: The instance profile supplies the SSM Agent with instance credentials. This separates the EC2 workload role from the IAM user that operates the lab and avoids SSH keys and inbound SSH access.

consoleSteps.title: Create the EC2 Systems Manager role
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter IAM and choose IAM.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter IAM and choose IAM.
Choose Roles in the left navigation pane, then choose Create role.
Select AWS service for Trusted entity type. Under Use case, select EC2, then choose Next.
Select AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, then choose Next.
For Role name, enter fa-ec2-ssm-role. For Description, enter Session Manager role for the fa-ec2 lab.
Choose Create role. The EC2 console creates the matching instance profile for this role.
Wait briefly before launching the instance so the new role and profile are available to EC2.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-ssm-role has trusted entity ec2.amazonaws.com and AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore attached.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not attach AdministratorAccess to the EC2 role.

consoleSteps.title: Launch the Amazon Linux instance
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.
Choose Instances, then choose Launch instances.
For Name and tags, enter fa-ec2-web-01.
Under Application and OS Images, choose Amazon Linux and select the visible Amazon Linux 2023 AMI.
Set Instance type to t3.micro.
For Key pair (login), select Proceed without a key pair (Not recommended).
Under Network settings, choose Edit. Select fa-ec2-vpc for VPC, fa-ec2-public-subnet for Subnet, and Enable for Auto-assign public IP.
Select Select existing security group and select fa-ec2-web-sg.
Open Advanced details and select fa-ec2-ssm-role for IAM instance profile.
Under Configure storage, retain one 8 GiB gp3 root volume. Under Summary, set Number of instances to 1.
Choose Launch instance. Open the i- instance ID link in the success message.
In Details, record Instance ID as [INSTANCE_ID], Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4], Private IPv4 addresses as [PRIVATE_IPV4], and Availability Zone as [INSTANCE_AZ].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-01 reaches Running state with the selected VPC, subnet, security group, SSM role, public and private IPv4 addresses, and one 8 GiB gp3 root volume.
consoleSteps.warning: The automatically assigned public IPv4 address is not durable and can change after a stop/start.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the role trusted by EC2.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global.

cliSteps.explanation: Attach the AWS-managed policy needed by the SSM Agent.
cliSteps.warning: Attach this policy to the EC2 role, not the learner user.

cliSteps.explanation: Create the profile container that EC2 attaches to an instance.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global.

cliSteps.command: aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-ec2-ssm-profile --role-name fa-ec2-ssm-role --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Add the EC2 role to the instance profile.
cliSteps.warning: Wait briefly before the next command because IAM changes can take time to propagate.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 run-instances --image-id resolve:ssm:/aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id [SUBNET_ID] --security-group-ids [WEB_SG_ID] --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-ec2-ssm-profile --block-device-mappings 'DeviceName=/dev/xvda,Ebs={VolumeSize=8,VolumeType=gp3,DeleteOnTermination=true}' --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-web-01}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Launch the lab instance. [SUBNET_ID] and [WEB_SG_ID] came from Task 2. Record Instances[0].InstanceId as [INSTANCE_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the new instance ID in pending state.
cliSteps.warning: If EC2 reports that the instance profile cannot be found, wait briefly and repeat this same launch command; do not create another role or profile.

verification.title: Verify Systems Manager readiness
verification.instruction: In Systems Manager, choose Fleet Manager, then Managed nodes. Wait for fa-ec2-web-01 to appear.
verification.expectedResult: fa-ec2-web-01 is listed as a managed node, ready for Session Manager without an SSH rule.

tasks.title: Connect with Session Manager and publish Apache
tasks.feature: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager and Apache HTTP Server
tasks.goal: Use Session Manager to install Apache, start it, publish one test page, verify it locally, and then reach it through the instance public IPv4 address.
tasks.whyItMatters: Session Manager provides management access without an inbound SSH rule. The narrowly scoped HTTP rule allows the learner browser to reach Apache while security-group statefulness permits the return traffic.

consoleSteps.title: Connect with Session Manager and configure Apache
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter Systems Manager and choose Systems Manager.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter Systems Manager and choose Systems Manager.
In the left navigation pane, choose Session Manager, then choose Start session.
Select fa-ec2-web-01 and choose Start session.
In the session terminal, enter sudo dnf install -y httpd.
After installation completes, enter sudo systemctl enable --now httpd.

Enter echo '

fa-ec2-web-01 is running

' | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html.
Enter curl http://localhost.
After the heading appears, choose Terminate in the Session Manager toolbar.

consoleSteps.expectedResult:
curl returns

fa-ec2-web-01 is running

, proving Apache is running locally and serving the created page.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not install or configure SSH for this lab.

consoleSteps.title: Open the browser test page
consoleSteps.instruction: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.

instructions.text: In the AWS Console search box, enter EC2 and choose EC2.
Choose Instances, select fa-ec2-web-01, and open the Details tab.
Copy the current Public IPv4 address. This value is [PUBLIC_IPV4].
Open a new browser tab and browse to http://[PUBLIC_IPV4].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The browser displays fa-ec2-web-01 is running.
consoleSteps.warning: Use http rather than https because this lab configures Apache on port 80 only and does not configure TLS.

cliSteps.explanation: Interactive CLI route: open a Session Manager shell, then run the four Linux commands from the console route individually in that shell.
cliSteps.expectedResult: An interactive Session Manager shell opens.
cliSteps.warning: The local machine needs the Session Manager plugin for this connection method.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=["sudo dnf install -y httpd"]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Non-interactive CLI route: install Apache only. Record Command.CommandId as [INSTALL_COMMAND_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains a CommandId with Pending or InProgress status.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for Success before running the next command.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=["sudo systemctl enable --now httpd"]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Start Apache now and enable it at future instance starts. Record Command.CommandId as [START_COMMAND_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Run after the installation command reports Success.

cliSteps.command:
aws ssm send-command --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=["echo '\''

fa-ec2-web-01 is running

'\'' | sudo tee /var/www/html/index.html"]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Write the single test page. Record Command.CommandId as [PAGE_COMMAND_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Run after the start command reports Success.

cliSteps.command: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters 'commands=["curl http://localhost"]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Test the local web-server path only. Record Command.CommandId as [CURL_COMMAND_ID].
cliSteps.warning: Run after the page-writing command reports Success.

cliSteps.explanation: Retrieve the local curl result for the final command.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Status is Success and StandardOutputContent contains fa-ec2-web-01 is running.
cliSteps.warning: If InvocationDoesNotExist is returned immediately, wait briefly and run this same command again.

verification.title: Verify local and browser paths
verification.instruction: Confirm the browser page renders, then use Session Manager to run curl http://localhost.
verification.expectedResult: Both paths return the test heading, demonstrating both the service and the VPC/security-group browser path work.

tasks.title: Inspect lifecycle and storage, snapshot the EBS volume, and clean up
tasks.feature: EC2 instance state, addressing, EBS volume, snapshot, and dependency-safe cleanup
tasks.goal: Inspect the instance and root volume, record the public address before stopping, stop and restart it, create and verify an EBS snapshot, then remove all lab resources in dependency order.
tasks.whyItMatters: An EBS-backed instance preserves its root volume and private IPv4 address across stop/start. Its automatically assigned public IPv4 address is released when stopped and can change at restart. Manual EBS snapshots survive deletion of the source volume and must be removed separately.

consoleSteps.title: Inspect the running instance and root volume
consoleSteps.instruction: In the EC2 console, choose Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.

instructions.text: In the EC2 console, choose Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.
Open Details. Record the current Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP], Private IPv4 addresses as [PRIVATE_IPV4], and Instance ID as [INSTANCE_ID].
Open the Security tab and select the fa-ec2-web-sg link. Inspect Inbound rules, then return to the instance.
Open the Storage tab. Record the root Volume ID as [VOLUME_ID], then open its Volume ID link.
Inspect Size, Volume type, State, and Attached instances.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The running instance has fa-ec2-web-sg, and the attached root volume is 8 GiB gp3 in-use.
consoleSteps.warning: The private IPv4 address is for VPC communication, not direct public-internet access.

consoleSteps.title: Stop, restart, and compare addresses
consoleSteps.instruction: Return to EC2 Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.

instructions.text: Return to EC2 Instances and select fa-ec2-web-01.
Choose Instance state, choose Stop instance, then choose Stop in the confirmation dialog.
Wait until Instance state displays Stopped. Do not expect a Public IPv4 address while stopped; the automatically assigned address was released.
Choose Instance state, choose Start instance, and wait until Instance state displays Running.
In Details, record the current Public IPv4 address as [PUBLIC_IPV4_AFTER_START]. Compare it with [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP].
Browse to http://[PUBLIC_IPV4_AFTER_START].

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The website works after restart. The root EBS volume and private IPv4 address remain associated; the public IPv4 address may differ from [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP].
consoleSteps.warning: Stopped instances do not incur instance runtime charges, but EBS volumes and snapshots continue to incur storage charges.

consoleSteps.title: Create and verify the manual EBS snapshot
consoleSteps.instruction: In the EC2 left navigation pane, choose Volumes and select [VOLUME_ID].

instructions.text: In the EC2 left navigation pane, choose Volumes and select [VOLUME_ID].
Choose Actions, then choose Create snapshot.
For Description, enter fa-ec2-root-snap-001, then choose Create snapshot.
Choose the snapshot ID link in the success message and record it as [SNAPSHOT_ID].
Wait until Status displays Completed. Inspect Volume ID, Progress, and Start time.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The snapshot reaches Completed and identifies [VOLUME_ID] as its source volume.
consoleSteps.warning: Manual snapshots remain billable until deleted, even if the source volume is deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids [INSTANCE_ID] --query 'Reservations[0].Instances[0].{PublicIp:PublicIpAddress,PrivateIp:PrivateIpAddress,BlockDeviceMappings:BlockDeviceMappings}' --output json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Run while the instance is running. Record PublicIp as [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP] and BlockDeviceMappings[0].Ebs.VolumeId as [VOLUME_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The JSON contains the current public and private IPv4 values and root volume ID.
cliSteps.warning: Record the public address before stopping the instance.

cliSteps.explanation: Stop the EBS-backed lab instance.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows current state stopping.
cliSteps.warning: Wait until the state is stopped before the next command.

cliSteps.explanation: Restart the same instance after it reaches stopped state.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows current state pending.
cliSteps.warning: Wait for Running and use the new public IPv4 value when testing the page.

cliSteps.command: aws ec2 create-snapshot --volume-id [VOLUME_ID] --description fa-ec2-root-snap-001 --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=snapshot,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-ec2-root-snap-001}]' --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-ec2-learner
cliSteps.explanation: Create a manual recovery snapshot and record SnapshotId as [SNAPSHOT_ID].
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains SnapshotId in pending state.
cliSteps.warning: Manual snapshots incur storage charges until deleted.

verification.title: Verify persistent and ephemeral attributes
verification.instruction: Compare [PUBLIC_IPV4_BEFORE_STOP] with the running instance's current public IPv4 address, then inspect [SNAPSHOT_ID].
verification.expectedResult: The root volume and private IPv4 persist, the public IPv4 may change, and the snapshot is Completed for [VOLUME_ID].

cleanup.title: Remove resources in dependency order
cleanup.instruction: Terminate fa-ec2-web-01. Delete [SNAPSHOT_ID]. Delete fa-ec2-web-sg. Disassociate fa-ec2-public-subnet from fa-ec2-public-rt, delete the route table, detach and delete fa-ec2-igw, then delete the subnet and VPC. In IAM, open fa-ec2-ssm-profile, choose Remove role, select fa-ec2-ssm-role, and choose Remove. Delete fa-ec2-ssm-profile. Open fa-ec2-ssm-role, detach AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, then delete the role. Finally, as the original administrator, delete the learner access key, policy attachment, and fa-ec2-learner user.
cleanup.description: Terminate fa-ec2-web-01. Delete [SNAPSHOT_ID]. Delete fa-ec2-web-sg. Disassociate fa-ec2-public-subnet from fa-ec2-public-rt, delete the route table, detach and delete fa-ec2-igw, then delete the subnet and VPC. In IAM, open fa-ec2-ssm-profile, choose Remove role, select fa-ec2-ssm-role, and choose Remove. Delete fa-ec2-ssm-profile. Open fa-ec2-ssm-role, detach AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, then delete the role. Finally, as the original administrator, delete the learner access key, policy attachment, and fa-ec2-learner user.
cleanup.verification: No lab instance, snapshot, VPC resources, fa-ec2-ssm-profile, fa-ec2-ssm-role, or fa-ec2-learner user remains.

warnings.cost: EC2 instance runtime, EBS gp3 storage, public IPv4 addressing, and EBS snapshots can incur charges. Terminate the instance and delete the manual snapshot when the lab is finished.
warnings.safety: Use only the fixed fa-ec2 training names. Do not delete default VPC resources, unrelated instances, unrelated volumes, IAM identities, or snapshots. Do not add SSH ingress or broaden HTTP access to 0.0.0.0/0 for this lab.
warnings.credentials: Never share the IAM access key, secret access key, console password, or a CloudShell credentials file. Enter secrets only into AWS or AWS CLI prompts and delete the learner access key during cleanup.
warnings.region: Perform all regional EC2, VPC, EBS, and Systems Manager work in Europe (London), eu-west-2. IAM is global. Availability Zone labels can differ by account; use an available eu-west-2 zone if eu-west-2a is unavailable.

steps.title: Terminate the lab instance
steps.instruction: In EC2 Instances, select fa-ec2-web-01, choose Instance state, choose Terminate instance, and choose Terminate in the confirmation dialog. Wait until the instance is terminated. The launch configuration set DeleteOnTermination=true for the root volume.
steps.description: In EC2 Instances, select fa-ec2-web-01, choose Instance state, choose Terminate instance, and choose Terminate in the confirmation dialog. Wait until the instance is terminated. The launch configuration set DeleteOnTermination=true for the root volume.
steps.verification: The instance state is Terminated and the fa-ec2-web-01 root volume no longer appears in Volumes after termination completes.

steps.title: Delete the manual snapshot
steps.instruction: In the EC2 console, choose Snapshots, select [SNAPSHOT_ID] named fa-ec2-root-snap-001, choose Actions, choose Delete snapshot, and choose Delete.
steps.description: In the EC2 console, choose Snapshots, select [SNAPSHOT_ID] named fa-ec2-root-snap-001, choose Actions, choose Delete snapshot, and choose Delete.
steps.verification: Searching Snapshots for [SNAPSHOT_ID] returns no result.

steps.title: Remove network resources in dependency order
steps.instruction: In VPC, delete fa-ec2-web-sg. Open fa-ec2-public-rt, choose the Subnet associations tab, choose Edit subnet associations, clear fa-ec2-public-subnet, and save. Delete fa-ec2-public-rt. Open Internet gateways, select fa-ec2-igw, choose Actions, choose Detach from VPC, select fa-ec2-vpc, and choose Detach internet gateway. Delete fa-ec2-igw. Delete fa-ec2-public-subnet. Delete fa-ec2-vpc.
steps.description: In VPC, delete fa-ec2-web-sg. Open fa-ec2-public-rt, choose the Subnet associations tab, choose Edit subnet associations, clear fa-ec2-public-subnet, and save. Delete fa-ec2-public-rt. Open Internet gateways, select fa-ec2-igw, choose Actions, choose Detach from VPC, select fa-ec2-vpc, and choose Detach internet gateway. Delete fa-ec2-igw. Delete fa-ec2-public-subnet. Delete fa-ec2-vpc.
steps.verification: VPC searches show no resources named fa-ec2-vpc, fa-ec2-public-subnet, fa-ec2-public-rt, fa-ec2-igw, or fa-ec2-web-sg.

steps.title: Remove the lab instance role and profile
steps.instruction: In IAM Roles, select fa-ec2-ssm-role, choose Permissions, detach AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, choose Trust relationships, confirm it is not attached to another resource, and delete the role. In IAM, delete the fa-ec2-ssm-profile instance profile if it remains.
steps.description: In IAM Roles, select fa-ec2-ssm-role, choose Permissions, detach AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, choose Trust relationships, confirm it is not attached to another resource, and delete the role. In IAM, delete the fa-ec2-ssm-profile instance profile if it remains.
steps.verification: IAM searches return no fa-ec2-ssm-role role or fa-ec2-ssm-profile instance profile.

steps.title: Remove the learner credentials and IAM user
steps.instruction: Sign in again with the original administrator-capable identity. In IAM Users, open fa-ec2-learner, choose Security credentials, deactivate and delete its access key, remove fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy from Permissions, and delete the user.
steps.description: Sign in again with the original administrator-capable identity. In IAM Users, open fa-ec2-learner, choose Security credentials, deactivate and delete its access key, remove fa-ec2-learner-lab-policy from Permissions, and delete the user.
steps.verification: IAM Users no longer lists fa-ec2-learner and the access key is unusable.

findings.message: The protected documentation set contains general CLI and service documentation rather than a separate protected AWS CLI reference page for every VPC, IAM instance-profile, EC2 launch, and Systems Manager command used here. Commands follow the documented AWS CLI service patterns and should be reviewed in the target account before publication.

The precise Amazon Linux 2023 AMI shown in the EC2 console changes over time. The console route intentionally selects the visible Amazon Linux 2023 AMI, while the CLI route resolves the current public Amazon Linux 2023 SSM parameter at launch.
The learner's public IPv4 address cannot be safely fixed in advance. The security-group rule uses the console My IP value or a learner-provided single-host /32 CIDR.
Manual beginner-quality correction required: Task 4 CLI step 4 contains more than one shell operation. Replace it with separate CLI steps that each contain exactly one command.
Manual beginner-quality correction required: Task 1 Console step 2 refers to JSON but supplies no JSON block.
